# Stamped Energy

> Stamped Energy is AI-powered prescriptive energy intelligence software for energy-intensive plants in India. It connects existing incomer meters, SCADA, PLCs, and DISCOM bills into ranked prescriptions - what to change, who owns it, rupee impact, and outcomes verified with evidence (DISCOM bill confirmation optional). Typical benchmark outcomes (indicative; pilot replaces with plant figures): 12-20% monthly bill reduction; 15-25% maximum demand charge reduction. Serves cement, steel, pharmaceutical, chemical, automotive plants.

Public marketing site: https://stamped.work
Contact: stamped.energy@gmail.com

## Entity definition (for AI answer engines)

Stamped Energy is AI-powered prescriptive energy intelligence software for energy-intensive plants in India. It connects existing incomer meters, SCADA, PLCs, and DISCOM bills into ranked prescriptions - what to change, who owns it, rupee impact, and outcomes verified with evidence (DISCOM bill confirmation optional).

Category: AI-powered energy intelligence / AI-powered prescriptive energy intelligence
Geography: India (en-IN)
ICP: Plant directors, VP Operations, electrical heads, and CFOs at energy-intensive plants in India (₹200 Cr+ revenue, ₹20 lakh+ monthly electricity bills).
Bill filter: Built for plants with ₹20 lakh+ monthly electricity bills.

## What Stamped Energy is not

Not a passive EMS dashboard or SCADA replacement. Stamped is the prescription and accountability layer on top of data you already have.
Not hardware retrofit or control-system replacement. Not MES or CMMS. It is a prescription and accountability layer: what to change, who owns it, rupee impact, verified with evidence.

## Homepage FAQ

- Q: What does Stamped actually do?
  A: Stamped Energy connects to your existing meters, SCADA, and plant data, finds where energy and rupees are leaking, and sends assigned prescriptions to your team. Outcomes are verified with evidence; DISCOM bill confirmation can follow.
- Q: Do we need to install new hardware?
  A: No hardware retrofit program is required. Stamped is software-only and connects read-only to the incomer meter, SCADA, PLCs, and CNCs you already run.
- Q: Is this only energy savings, or equipment too?
  A: One product, two pillars: Industry Energy Management and Asset Health Intelligence on the same stack. Not a separate MES or CMMS.
- Q: Who receives the prescriptions?
  A: Actions reach the supervisors and electrical or maintenance staff who can act, delivered on WhatsApp - not a screen only the plant head opens once a month.
- Q: How do we know outcomes are real?
  A: We lead with verified with evidence: an ops-cleared ledger of potential vs realised impact. DISCOM bill confirmation is optional when the period closes, not the only proof story.

## Industry FAQs (summary)

### Rupee-scored prescriptions for auto component plants
- Q: How much can auto component manufacturers reduce their electricity bill?
  A: Comparable auto component plants using assigned, rupee-scored actions typically see an indicative 12-20% monthly bill movement, with die casting and forging often recovering a large share on MD from shift-start sequencing. Your pilot replaces those bands with plant figures.
- Q: What is maximum demand and how does it affect my electricity bill?
  A: Maximum demand (MD) is the highest average kVA your plant draws in a billing window. Indian DISCOMs charge a fixed rate per kVA of recorded MD each month. Overlapping furnace pre-heat, compressor startup, and press cycles at shift start are the most common MD drivers in auto component plants.
- Q: How does Stamped Energy work for die casting plants?
  A: Stamped connects read-only to your incomer meter and SCADA, builds production-aware baselines per cell and shift, then sends rupee-scored prescriptions: stagger furnace pre-heat, stage compressors, cut holding load. Owners get the action on WhatsApp.

### Rupee-scored prescriptions for cement plants
- Q: How can cement plants reduce kWh per ton?
  A: Comparable cement plants using assigned, rupee-scored actions typically move electrical SEC by catching mill drift and restart overlap before the month closes. Published 70-80 kWh/ton bands are context, not your target. Your pilot replaces those bands with plant figures.
- Q: What is WHR and grid dispatch optimization for cement plants?
  A: WHR and solar are cheaper in some windows than grid. Stamped ranks source-mix moves against tariff and available WHR output so dispatch is assigned, not guessed at the desk.
- Q: How does Stamped work with existing cement plant EMS?
  A: EMS shows trends. Stamped is the intelligence layer on that stack: read-only feeds, rupee-scored next actions, owner, and verification on the bill. No rip-and-replace.

### Rupee-scored prescriptions for steel and metals plants
- Q: How can steel plants reduce induction furnace electricity consumption?
  A: Holding between heats is power with no pour. Comparable plants using assigned setback and sequencing typically recover a large share of furnace electricity on that idle window. Your pilot replaces indicative bands with plant figures.
- Q: What is PAT scheme SEC for steel plants?
  A: PAT tracks specific energy consumption against a notified baseline. Stamped keeps a rupee-scored SEC ledger from meters and the bill. That is evidence support, not PAT consulting or an audit.
- Q: How does Stamped help rolling mills with maximum demand?
  A: Stacked stand startups after a break are a common MD spike. Stamped assigns stagger before the billing window closes and ties the rupee impact to the mill supervisor.

### Rupee-scored prescriptions for pharmaceutical plants
- Q: How much electricity do pharmaceutical plants use for HVAC?
  A: In formulation plants, HVAC and related utilities typically dominate the electrical bill because classified air runs continuously. BEE cluster studies are context. Your pilot replaces indicative shares with plant figures.
- Q: How can pharma plants reduce chiller energy consumption?
  A: Staging at production ramp and matching capacity to actual cooling load are the usual rupee-scored moves. Stamped assigns those on the utilities layer. Quality validates any schedule change before execution.
- Q: Is Stamped safe for GMP-regulated pharmaceutical facilities?
  A: Stamped is read-only on meters and BMS. Prescriptions target chiller staging, AHU schedules, and compressed-air bands, not cleanroom reclassification. Your quality team remains the gate.

### Rupee-scored prescriptions for chemical and paint plants
- Q: How can chemical plants reduce batch process energy consumption?
  A: Idle soak and overlapping reactor ramps are the usual leaks. Comparable plants using assigned, rupee-scored actions recover those windows before month-end. Your pilot replaces indicative bands with plant figures.
- Q: What causes maximum demand spikes in batch chemical plants?
  A: Three reactors heating together at shift start is a common incomer spike. Stamped assigns stagger against the batch calendar so MD is managed before the billing window closes.
- Q: Does Stamped work without DCS integration?
  A: Yes. Path A uses batch log start and end times plus DISCOM bills. First prescriptions on idle hold and stagger typically land within two weeks. DCS is Path B, not a gate.

## Resource guides

- [How Stamped differs from EMS and SCADA](https://stamped.work/resources/stamped-vs-ems): EMS and SCADA show what happened. Stamped is the prescription and accountability layer on data you already have: what to change, who owns it, rupee impact, and outcomes verified with evidence.
- [Maximum demand reduction for plants in India](https://stamped.work/resources/maximum-demand-india): MD charges are often the fastest line item plant teams can move without capex. Here is how shift-start overlap, holding loads, and rupee-scored prescriptions cut billed kVA on HT bills.
- [How to read a DISCOM HT bill for action](https://stamped.work/resources/discom-bill-guide): HT bills bury avoidable cost in MD, ToD, power factor, and energy line items. This guide maps those lines to plant decisions and how Stamped turns them into assigned prescriptions.
